subject: Commercial options for OrbitHealth onramp: migration credits, SLA alignment, and rollout runbook
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-27T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Commercial options for OrbitHealth onramp: migration credits, SLA alignment, and rollout runbook

Hi Elena — great talking to you and Oliver yesterday. I wanted to put a concrete commercial proposal on the table so your procurement and engineering teams can evaluate trade-offs across pricing, credits, and SLA commitments. High level: we can match the near-term economics you shared and add a migration credit bucket plus a short dedicated pilot to reduce risk.

Offer summary (initial):
- Term: 12 months committed consumption (monthly invoiced)
- List discount: 18% off list for the committed term
- Migration credits: $60,000 one-time credit applied to usage over first 90 days (can be used to offset tokens or private deployment onboarding fees)
- Pilot: 2-week Dedicated pilot environment (no charge) to validate latency and runtime parity
- SLA: 99.9% platform uptime for production routes; credits available for SLA breaches per contract schedule

Conditions and notes: we can match a competitor’s migration credit bucket if you share the competitor’s contract or credit schedule (redacted OK) so we align economics. Migration credit use is flexible but not refundable (applies only to Redwood usage billing). I’m attaching a short migration credit schedule and a technical rollout runbook for your ops team to review.

Next steps: can you confirm the procurement questions below so we can draft a contract and DocuSign?
- Will OrbitHealth require a dedicated Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for initial onboarding, or will a Dedicated pool + VPC peering be acceptable?
- Any specific indemnity or data residency clauses beyond our standard enterprise addendum?

If this looks reasonable I’ll have our legal and finance prepare a marked-up term sheet and a DocuSign envelope for signature.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
pri...@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: redwood-migration-credit-schedule.pdf, technical-rollout-runbook.pdf

From: Elena Park <elena.park@orbithealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@orbithealth.com>, procurement@orbithealth.com
Date: 2027-08-27T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial options for OrbitHealth onramp: migration credits, SLA alignment, and rollout runbook

Hi Priya — thanks for the summary. A few clarifying questions from procurement and engineering before we move to a term sheet:

1) Migration credits: can you provide an amortization schedule that shows how credits are applied to monthly invoices vs. one-off onboarding fees? Are credits transferable between OrbitHealth business units?
2) Refundability: are any of the credits refundable if we terminate early or not use them within 90 days?
3) SLA specifics: what is the credit calculation for partial outages (token-level vs. route-level)? We need the precise formula to present to legal.
4) Runtime parity: our infra team needs confirmation that the model variants you serve will be bit-for-bit compatible with the models we currently run (we’re using a customized quantized variant today). If not, what uplift in per-token cost should we plan for?

I’ve attached our internal procurement checklist (RFP) for reference. Please loop in your Solutions Engineering owner for the runtime parity details.

— Elena
Elena Park
Head of Procurement, OrbitHealth
elena.park@orbithealth.com

Attachment: OrbitHealth-RFP-Aug2027.pdf

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-27T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial options for OrbitHealth onramp: migration credits, SLA alignment, and rollout runbook

Thanks Elena — good questions. Short answers up front, details below and I’ve attached a worked migration-plan spreadsheet.

1) Credits amortization: credits are consumed against invoice line items in priority order: onboarding fees -> private deployment setup -> usage (tokens). Practically this means if you use the pilot and incur setup fees, the credit first offsets those charges. Any remaining credit reduces monthly usage invoices until consumed or until 90 days. Credits are not transferable between legally separate entities without our prior written consent.

2) Refundability: credits are not refundable. If you terminate early we can discuss a pro-rated reconciliation but the standard offer is non-refundable because the credit is applied as a commercial concession against operational onboarding costs.

3) SLA calculation: credit = (minutes_down / total SLA minutes) * monthly committed fee * SLA-penalty-factor. We’ll include the exact clause in the term sheet; Laura will insert the legal language. For route-level partial degradations (e.g., high-tail latency) we offer graded credits tied to token-success and latency SLOs — we’ll map the thresholds in the contract.

4) Runtime parity & cost uplift: short version — we support a variety of quantized runtimes; in many cases there’s parity at functional level but you may see a token-cost uplift of ~6–15% depending on model size and sequence length distribution. Marcus has a quick estimate and pilot plan below.

Link to HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/987654321/oh-2027-0342
DocuSign template (draft): https://www.docusign.com/en/us/sign?envelopeId=ABCD-1234-ORBIT

Attachments: redwood-migration-plan.xlsx

If that works I’ll ask legal to issue a term sheet and include a clause that references the competitor credit schedule if you provide it (we don’t need the competitor docs beyond the credit schedule and expiry).

— Priya

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbithealth.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-28T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial options for OrbitHealth onramp: migration credits, SLA alignment, and rollout runbook

Hi Elena — Marcus on the SE side. Quick technical notes to help OrbitHealth’s infra team assess runtime parity: 

- We can run your current quantized variant in a Dedicated pool; if the variant uses custom kernels we’ll need to validate during the pilot (2 weeks) but we have a 3-stage validation flow: unit inference checks -> throughput stress -> production-like traffic validation.
- Based on the model family and your avg seq length, the expected per-token cost uplift is about 8% (range 5–12%). I’ll provide a short benchmark showing baseline token cost vs. Redwood-managed inference with prefix caching and continuous batching enabled.
- Staging offer: we’ll provision a mirrored staging cluster and share a telemetry dashboard and sample traces so you can compare latency percentiles. The pilot includes one remediation window and a rollback playbook if throughput or latency targets aren’t met.

If you’d like, we can run a 24-48 hour compatibility check during the week of Sept 6 to give you a tighter uplift estimate.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Quote: "We’ll keep the pilot environment locked at staging latency SLOs so you can validate before committing to traffic."

From: Elena Park <elena.park@orbithealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Shaw <oliver.shaw@orbithealth.com>, procurement@orbithealth.com
Date: 2027-08-29T10:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial options for OrbitHealth onramp: migration credits, SLA alignment, and rollout runbook

Thanks Priya and Marcus — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from legal/procurement: 

- We need the migration credits represented explicitly in the contract (term sheet language) with a clear expiry date. Please include an example clause that shows the $60k credit and the 90-day expiry.
- SLA penalties: procurement wants a defined cap and formula (we understand graded credits but need the math in the contract).
- Pilot acceptance criteria: we’ll provide a short test harness; please confirm the acceptance gating (latency p95, error-rate threshold, and throughput).

Assuming those are in the term sheet we’re prepared to run the compatibility check Sept 6 and aim to complete the pilot by Sept 20. If everything lines up legal will ask for the credit clause to be in the signed contract.

Can you have a marked term sheet with the credit clause and pilot acceptance criteria to us by EOD Aug 31? We’ll review and route to legal.

— Elena

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@orbithealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-30T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Commercial options for OrbitHealth onramp: migration credits, SLA alignment, and rollout runbook

Elena — confirmed. We’ll get a marked term sheet in your inbox by EOD Aug 31 that: (a) includes the $60,000 migration credit clause with 90-day expiry language, (b) spells out the exact SLA credit math and monthly cap, and (c) defines pilot acceptance gates (p95 latency <= 250ms, error-rate < 0.5%, and sustained throughput >= agreed baseline).

We’ve penciled in Sept 6 for the 24-48 hour compatibility run — Marcus will own scheduling and telemetry. I’ll also send the DocuSign envelope and a draft SOW referencing the credit clause once legal finalizes the term sheet.

Thanks — Priya

Action items: Priya to send term sheet and DocuSign; Marcus to schedule compatibility run for week of Sept 6; OrbitHealth to share competitor credit schedule if they want a precise match.
